title: What the Orca remembers

is_this_you.pressure: When the water goes thin, the pod watches which way you face. You remember where the fish were the last bad year.
is_this_you.love: You range a whole coast and still come back to the same few voices.
is_this_you.cost: Grief rides on your back for weeks. You let it sink only when you are ready.

opener.text: In Chinese the orca is 虎鯨 (hǔjīng), the tiger whale [s19]. You were born in a Horse year, and the Tiger stands in the Horse's own trine of Tiger, Horse and Dog [s3]. Read that way, your animal's name carries your strongest ally inside it. You came into the water already wearing a tiger's name.

howto: Three parts. Swim them in any order.

tabs.label: The pod
tabs.intro: Deep Water underneath, and a running Fire on top.

rows.text: Scorpio is fixed Water, passionate and fiercely loyal once trust is given, able to focus deeply on one thing [s1] [s2]. The Horse is yang Fire, energetic and independent, hungry for new ground [s4] [s6]. The Horse in you wants to swim the whole coast tonight, while the Scorpio has already picked the one inlet worth the trip. You live in the pull between them.

Fish-eating resident orcas live in families led by the eldest female, and sons and daughters stay with their mothers for life [s7]. Each population keeps its own dialect of calls [s7]. Your people have a dialect too. Strangers hear the sound and miss the meaning, and you like it that way.
In 2018 an orca named Tahlequah carried her dead calf for 17 days and about 1,000 miles [s12]. You do not set a loss down on anyone else's schedule. Your pod has learned to slow down and stay close.

tabs.label: What the elders know
tabs.intro: The oldest one remembers where the salmon went.

rows.text: Orca females stop breeding and can live for decades after their last calf [s8] [s9]. A 2019 study found that a grandmother's presence raised her grandcalves' survival, most of all in years when salmon were scarce [s8]. In lean years the older females often lead the group to food [s9]. You keep the map of hard years for everyone.

At the Crozet Islands, young orcas first practise stranding on the beach at about four or five, and still need an adult female's help at five or six [s13]. You teach like that, slowly and over years. You stay close enough to pull your student back off the sand when the wave turns.
Expedition work, coaching, search and rescue and family firms all need someone who remembers the last bad season.

tabs.label: Who swims in your wake
tabs.intro: Three who swim in your line. One whose current runs against yours.
tabs.love_lead: In love you choose a pod and stay in it. The passion runs under a calm surface, and you still need room to range. Whoever loves you takes both the long silences and the sudden long swims. The Chinese pairings favour three.

easy.why: The Moon Bear (Cancer, Tiger year) carries the Tiger of your trine, and Cancer is Water like you [s3] [s1].
The Beluga (Pisces, Dog year) closes your trine of Tiger, Horse and Dog, and Pisces makes the third Water sign [s3] [s1].
The Snow Leopard (Scorpio, Goat year) shares your sign, and the Goat is the Horse's six-harmony partner [s3] [s1].

hard.why: The hard one is the Aardwolf (Taurus, Rat year): the Rat clashes with the Horse, and Taurus sits opposite Scorpio [s3] [s1].

story.k: The god of the offshore sea
story.text: The Ainu of Hokkaido tell of Repun Kamuy, the god of the offshore sea, who is sometimes shown as an orca [s16]. In one story he harpoons a whale and throws it ashore as a gift for a pious village, so that famine stays away [s16].

closing: Throw the big catch up onto the shore. Your people will eat well this winter, and they will know whose gift it was.
